THE PR BODY'S CENTRAL STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS TRUE -- I verified it in source rather than taking it, because it decides what my own DISAGREE costs. In scripts/lwb_lanes.py::_review_ok the `verdict != "AGREE"` branch tags rejection_kind 'other' and returns, and the staleness branch (reviewed_commit vs head_sha, tagging 'stale') sits ~30 lines BELOW it. independent_reviews' own docstring then states: 'Only staleness is routine churn from ordinary review rounds superseding each other; dissent and identity problems are not.' So a DISAGREE is classified 'other' irrespective of whether the commit it reviewed has been superseded, and an 'other' rejection is never outvoted by a later valid AGREE. CONSEQUENCE, STATED OPENLY BECAUSE IT IS THE COST OF THIS VERDICT: this record is unclearable in place, and #73 will need a re-cut exactly as #72 did. I am filing it anyway, because AGREE on a PR with a self-inflicted red required check would be a false attestation, and because the finding is NOT already fixed -- it is red on GitHub's runners as I write. But the repository should see the shape of this: the `_review_ok` ordering defect, which #73 deliberately scopes out, has now forced re-cuts of #72 and #73 back to back. THE CHEAPEST PATH IS TO FIX THAT ORDERING DEFECT FIRST, as its own scoped PR, before re-cutting this one; otherwise the next honest DISAGREE burns #74 too. A stale DISAGREE whose findings are provably fixed is churn, not dissent, and _review_ok cannot currently tell them apart.
